text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today as crude oil prices surged on geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Iran escalated attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, driving U.S. crude up sharply and pushing the global oil price to $126.55 per barrel — well above the $102 U.S. benchmark. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly translate to higher revenue and profit on barrels they sell, which is why the stock climbed alongside the commodity.

The two-week rally (up 15.6% since early October) reflects a broader shift in oil markets driven by supply concerns in a key chokepoint. Adding to the picture: tanker rates have surged, which means the actual cost to move and deliver physical oil is running roughly $38 per barrel higher than the headline price suggests — a dynamic that can squeeze some buyers but benefits producers with secure sales channels.
